newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates steady on exporters' demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates steady on exporters' demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates remained unchanged on Monday on demand from exporters and are likely to hover around these levels in the near term, dealers said.

"The prices remained stable as exporters are on the buying side," dealer Nasim Usman said. "Mill owners are also going for good-quality stocks and there are bright chances that the ginners would be able to unload most of their unsold stocks from the 1996/97 (July-June) crop."
Earlier, there were fears that the hangover from the 1996/97 crop would depress the prices of new crop due next month.
Dealers said there were still about 700,000 bales of unslold cotton from the 1996/97 crop.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was traded around 2,000 rupees ($49.39) per maund (37.32 kg), they said.
